title: What fine-tuning does and does not inject, and what it costs now

claims.text: Ovadia, Brief, Mishaeli and Elisha published Fine-Tuning or Retrieval? Comparing Knowledge Injection in LLMs, as a preprint in 2023 and at the 2024 conference on empirical methods in natural language processing, pages 237 to 250. They compare unsupervised fine-tuning with retrieval-augmented generation on knowledge-intensive tasks across several topics. While unsupervised fine-tuning offers some improvement, retrieval consistently outperforms it, both for knowledge encountered during pre-training and for new information. They find that the models struggle to learn new factual information through unsupervised fine-tuning, and suggest that exposing them to numerous variations of the same fact during training could alleviate the problem.

source.title: Oded Ovadia, Menachem Brief, Moshik Mishaeli and Oren Elisha, Fine-Tuning or Retrieval? Comparing Knowledge Injection in LLMs, EMNLP 2024, pages 237-250

claims.text: Hu, Shen and colleagues published LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models in 2021. Their premise is that as models grow, full fine-tuning that retrains all parameters becomes less feasible, and deploying independent instances of a fine-tuned model of 175 billion parameters is prohibitively expensive. The method freezes the pre-trained weights and injects trainable rank decomposition matrices into each layer. Compared with fine-tuning that model with the Adam optimiser, it reduces the number of trainable parameters by 10,000 times and the memory requirement on the accelerator by 3 times, performs on par with or better than fine-tuning in model quality across several models, has higher training throughput, and, unlike adapter layers, adds no additional inference latency.

source.title: Edward Hu, Yelong Shen and others, LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models, ICLR 2022

beats.broke: a model that behaves almost right invites the conclusion that it should be trained on your data, which is the most expensive available response and frequently addresses the wrong problem
beats.fix: separate what fine-tuning teaches from what it cannot reliably inject: reach for instructions, examples and retrieval first, and train only when the gap is in form rather than in facts
beats.cost: a fine-tuned model is a new artefact you own, version, evaluate and maintain, and the training was never the expensive part
beats.interview: what fine-tuning is for, what it is not for, and what to try before it
